references.text: Here are also mentioned tribal princes, one from each tribe in Israel, who were appointed to assist Moses with the census.
The princes of the Israelites, heads of their families, who were the tribal leaders and led those being mustered, brought their offerings.
Twelve staffs were gathered, one from each tribal leader, representing the heads of the tribes.
Moses, the priest Eleazar, and all the princes of the congregation went out to meet the army, corresponding to the delegation in Joshua.
Moses gave orders on the matter to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the heads of the tribes, which resembles the leadership structure here.
The same chapter confirms that the priest Phinehas and the princes received an answer from the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh.
Moses chose capable men from all Israel and appointed them as leaders over the people, as commanders of thousands and hundreds.
